facts.raw_span: A 31-year-old woman
presents with a 4-year history of recurrent painful ulcerations on both legs and feet
no personal or family history of vascular or autoimmune disease
denies arthralgia or other dermatologic symptoms
takes no medications
denies tobacco or illicit drug use
a reticular purplish livedo pattern is noted over both lower limbs
Multiple chronic, nonhealing ulcers are present over the lateral malleolus and the dorsum of the left foot
white atrophic scars on the lower legs and ankles
thrombophilia, hematologic malignancies, immune-mediated vasculitis, connective tissue diseases, arterial disease, vascular proliferations, diabetes, and medication-induced ulcers
A lesional skin biopsy was performed
